data.body:
From the PS-snapshot-calibrate critic round 4 (deepseek, LOW). (1) ddflow/infra/log/_parse.py _SNAP_SWEPT grows by one Path per events dir in a long-lived process: cap it. (2) _collect_stale_snapshots counts the current snapshot in the total but never evicts it, so an existing snapshot over a lowered snapshot_max_mb survives until the log changes: delete it when it alone exceeds the cap. Add a test for each.

Superseding note: the two findings above were fixed in PS-snapshot-calibrate. The 5th critic round raised two new LOW ones, deferred here: (a) _collect_stale_snapshots: total -= mine_size is skipped when mine.unlink() raises (use missing_ok / decrement outside the suppress); (b) the _SNAP_SWEPT bound is not atomic across threads (overshoot by the number of concurrent readers).

data.summary: Regression on branch ddflow/PS-snapshot-calibrate (3378f5b28), not on main. _GuardMixin._shard_meta (ddflow/infra/log/_guard.py:48) returns None when _snapshot_enabled() is false, so defaulting log.snapshot to false also turns off the per-shard facts cache used by the append path: tests/test_lamport_highwater.py::test_an_append_in_a_fresh_process_does_not_parse_every_shard reads 82 shards instead of <=3, test_an_append_continues_the_clock_and_leaves_a_mark leaves no mark, tests/test_log_scale.py::test_shardmeta_does_not_launder_a_same_length_rewrite gets meta None. The two knobs need separating: the marshal snapshot off must not switch ShardMeta off. Also regressed by the same default: tests/test_fsio_log.py (2 tests, _SNAP config needs snapshot=True) and tests/test_upgrade_apply_knobs.py::test_config_changes_operator_with_a_confirm_applies_it (knob_changed log.max_cached_events is refused without --confirm). All 6 pass at merge-base e7d53a7c6 and on main 4fadc519c. Probe: uv run pytest tests/test_lamport_highwater.py tests/test_log_scale.py tests/test_fsio_log.py -q on the branch.

CORRECTION by the reporter (ps-snapcal): the 'ok' in this bug's summary was printed by my own shell loop (`ddflow update ... >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo ok`), not by ddflow. What was actually observed: one exit 0 from `ddflow update --globs` run under the tree-derived identity (no --agent), after which the lease held changes.toml but not log.py, so the requested list was at most partly applied. Every refusal I saw printed its reason. The exit code of a refused CLI update was not measured separately. Reproduce that before fixing; this may be invalid as filed.
